findings.title: Installer identity is not checked on first link
findings.body: The new GitHub-user check never runs when no Integration row exists yet. OAuthLoginView records github_authenticated_user, but GitHubInstallation catches Integration.DoesNotExist and calls pipeline.next_step(), which creates the integration and organization link from the caller-supplied installation_id with no comparison to metadata sender. GitHub installation ids are enumerable and the installation webhook can arrive after this request, so an attacker who finishes any OAuth login can win that race and attach someone else's app installation to their Sentry org. Once that OrganizationIntegration exists, the later "already installed" branch blocks the real installer. The mismatch check has to fail closed until the webhook sender is known, including on this create path.

findings.title: Missing sender metadata crashes re-link
findings.body: The new comparison reads integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with no guard. build_integration only stores sender when pipeline state already has it, and older or webhook-incomplete Integration rows can be ACTIVE with zero OrganizationIntegrations — exactly the branch that reaches this line. A missing or non-dict sender raises KeyError instead of the installation-failed page, so a legitimate re-link 500s and cannot be completed.

findings.title: Installation-not-found test no longer hits that path
findings.body: test_installation_not_found stubs a 404 from /app/installations/{id} but then calls setup with state ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, which is not the pipeline signature (9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3). OAuthLoginView rejects the state and returns "Invalid installation request." before build_integration or the 404 handler runs. The assertion matches that generic error, so a regression in the installation-not-found path would still pass, and the old "The GitHub installation could not be found." contract is no longer covered.
